name: Local Group
tagline: The ~80-galaxy cluster the Milky Way calls home — a volume ~10 million light-years wide bound by shared gravity.

facts.label: Two giants
facts.value: Milky Way + Andromeda dominate its mass

facts.label: Sub-groups
facts.value: MW satellites and the M31 swarm

history: The Local Group is the galaxy cluster we live in — a small, gravity-bound gathering of some eighty known galaxies centred between its two giants, the Milky Way and Andromeda, which carry nearly all its mass. The rest are dwarfs: the Magellanic Clouds, the M31 satellite swarm, the faint spheroidals and the isolated irregulars scattered between them. The group is not expanding with the universe — its members orbit their shared centre of mass, and its two giants are on a collision course ~4.5 billion years hence.
